questions.question: What are Letta's three memory tiers?
options: Core, recall, archival
Working, episodic, semantic
RAM, swap, and virtual memory
Cache, KV store, archival
questions.explanation: Letta uses core (always visible), recall (conversation history), and archival (external) tiers.

questions.question: Which production problem does sleep-time compute target?
options: Block bloat from unlimited block_append calls hitting the character limit
Tail latency from doing memory consolidation on the critical path
Poisoned consolidation from attacker-reachable content entering core memory
Silent drift where the primary agent never sees a rewritten block underneath it
questions.explanation: Sleep-time moves prune/summarize/reconcile off the user-facing path, so primary responses stay fast.

questions.question: Which property is NOT a memory block field in Letta?
options: label (short identifier)
value (block content)
embedding_model_version
limit (character cap)
questions.explanation: Blocks carry id, label, value, limit, description; embedding model version is not part of the block schema.

questions.question: Why can the sleep-time agent run a stronger model than the primary?
options: It receives a private API key that bypasses the primary agent's rate limits
It is exempt from the per-request rate limits the primary model faces
Memory consolidation writes cost roughly half the tokens of a normal turn
It is off the critical path, so it is not latency-constrained
questions.explanation: Because it does not block user responses, the sleep-time agent can be slower and more expensive.

questions.question: What pattern do the Human and Persona blocks generalize to?
options: Arbitrary user-defined typed editable blocks (Task, Project, Safety, ...)
Vector embeddings stored alongside the core block for semantic retrieval
JSON-RPC channels used to synchronize state between the primary and sleep-time agents
OS-style processes, each with its own memory space and scheduler priority
questions.explanation: Letta generalizes the two MemGPT blocks to any user-defined block with id, label, value, limit, description.

questions.question: What is silent drift in this pattern?
options: The sleep-time agent silently exhausting the disk quota reserved for archival storage before the primary agent's very next turn
A primary agent never seeing that the sleep-time agent rewrote a block underneath it; fix with versioning and visible diffs
An upgraded embedding model changing vector similarity scores between sessions without flagging the change
Rate-limit jitter causing sleep-time consolidation to run on an unpredictable schedule
questions.explanation: Versioning blocks and surfacing diffs in the trace makes sleep-time rewrites visible to the primary loop.
